description: How does Zn fertilizer application (soil, foliar, and soil+foliar) affect grain Zn concentration in wheat? The goal is agronomic biofortification to address Zn deficiency in human nutrition. Based on Hui et al. 2025 (Nature Communications 16:3913).
intervention: Zinc fertilizer application (ZnSO4, ZnO, Zn-EDTA, etc. via soil, foliar, or combined)
typical_effect_size: +29% for soil, +55% for foliar, +62% for soil+foliar
moderators: Spraying timing (booting, heading, flowering, grain filling)
extraction_priorities: 1. CRITICAL: Extract EVERY treatment combination separately -- no pooling across Zn rates, methods, or timings
2. Control = no Zn application (CK), treatment = with Zn application
3. If factorial design (Zn rate x timing x form), extract each combination vs its control
4. Get variance (SE/SD/LSD) and sample size (n) -- many papers use LSD
5. Record the Zn application rate, method, and fertilizer type for each observation
tc_confusion_warnings: Control is the zero-Zn treatment, not untreated plants
Some papers use multiple Zn rates -- extract EACH rate vs the zero-Zn control
Foliar vs soil application are different treatments, not replicates
LSD is very common in agronomy -- extract it as a variance measure
notes: LSD can be converted to SD using: SD = LSD * sqrt(n) / t_crit. Many papers report LSD at 5% significance.
